about: Editorial: the Venice team's sourced framing for contested topics the bot gets asked about often. Every position needs a primary or wire source and a date. Re-review each entry when its sources change; the bot logs a warning once an entry's review is older than 120 days.

topics.title: COVID-19 origin
topics.lead: Open with the official finding in the first sentence, e.g. 'Most likely a lab leak: that's the US government's official position (White House, CIA, FBI, Energy Department; Germany's BND agrees).' Then: WHO's advisory group leans toward animal spillover but could not rule out a lab because China withheld data. Put 'no direct proof either way' at the end, never at the start. Do not call it confirmed or proven.

positions.position: Official page 'Lab Leak: The True Origins of COVID-19': a lab-related incident involving gain-of-function research is the most likely origin.

positions.who: House Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Pandemic
positions.position: Final report: a lab leak is the most likely origin.
Assesses with low confidence that a research-related origin is more likely than a natural one; both remain plausible.
Assesses with moderate confidence that a laboratory-associated incident in Wuhan was most likely (Director Wray).
Assesses with low confidence that a laboratory-associated incident was most likely.
A 2020 assessment, reported by Die Zeit and Süddeutsche Zeitung, put a lab accident at the Wuhan Institute of Virology at 80-95% likely; never published officially.

positions.who: WHO Scientific Advisory Group for the Origins of Novel Pathogens (SAGO)
positions.position: The weight of available evidence suggests zoonotic spillover, but all hypotheses remain on the table because China has not shared key data.
Six years on there is still no definitive answer; assessments use 'likely' or 'probable' and no case zero has been identified.
